quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes inside an intersection.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check for other drivers in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Do not change lanes inside an intersection. Before changing lanes, always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: If your car's rear end starts skidding to the left, you should:

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car starts to skid, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This helps straighten your car.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a right turn. It is unsafe and illegal to turn right at this intersection.

questions.question: The best way to avoid a dangerous situation while driving is to:

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always keep your eyes focused ahead of your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always be aware of what is happening around your vehicle. Watch the front, sides, and rear. This helps you see problems and react by changing speed or position.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Start to prepare to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Sound a sharp blast of your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
questions.explanation: Sound a sharp horn blast when a child or pedestrian is about to step into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: What do defensive drivers think about?

options.text: Other drivers will do the right thing.
What other drivers might do and prepare to react.
They expect no breaks and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: What other drivers might do and prepare to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive drivers expect problems from other drivers and are ready to react to their mistakes.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, check for a gap in traffic, adjust your speed to match traffic, signal, and:

options.text: Expect traffic to let you in since you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to clear before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: Find a gap, speed up to match traffic, signal, and merge when safe. Do not expect other drivers to clear the lane for you.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Stay off the brakes and let the car slide to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly on snow or ice. The ABS will pump the brakes faster than you can.

questions.question: You are driving in the left lane with two lanes in your direction. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. If the driver behind you wants to drive faster, you should:

options.text: Stay in your lane so you don't block traffic.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let vehicles pass.
Move into the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to drive fast, pass, or turn left. Use the right lane when driving slower than surrounding traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: You should always travel at:

options.text: The speed of vehicles around you.
The speed limit.
A speed that fits road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: A speed that fits road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed depends on road conditions, weather, and the legal speed limit. Never drive above the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Does not increase crash risk.
Increases your ability to react to hazards.
Often leads to risky decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often leads to risky decisions.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to dangerous decisions.

questions.question: Your license can be suspended if you are under 21 and drive with a blood alcohol level of:

options.text: 0.15 percent or more.
0.08 percent or more.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 cannot have any alcohol. Any trace of alcohol will result in harsh penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: If you are driving on a highway next to a single broken white line:

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
Slow down and proceed carefully.
Stop and wait until the light stops flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a full stop and proceed when safe.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to areas where animals, people, and vehicles cross traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Be ready for traffic to merge into your lane.
Always stop.
Divided highway ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for traffic to merge into your lane.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign means traffic will merge from the right. Be ready to let them in safely.

questions.question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep your wheels facing straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your wheels right toward the road edge. This helps the car roll off the road if the brakes fail.

questions.question: Broken yellow lines are used to:

options.text: Mark no-passing zones.
Separate lanes going the same direction.
Separate lanes going opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes going opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going opposite directions. Dashed yellow lines mean passing is allowed when safe.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water pools on the road. At speeds above 35 mph, tires lose contact with the road and slide like water skis.

questions.question: When you merge onto the freeway, you should be driving:

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
The posted speed limit for the freeway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, match the speed of traffic on the freeway.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Use only your rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
Use only your left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Check several times if needed. Watch both the traffic ahead and the traffic in the lane next to you.

questions.question: When using a roundabout, drivers should:

options.text: Yield to entering traffic.
Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Drive in a clockwise direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection with no traffic signal. Traffic moves counterclockwise around a central island. Enter from the right and yield to traffic already in the roundabout. Follow the circle to the right until you reach your exit.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A divided highway is ending.
A divided highway is starting.
The road ahead will be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is starting.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you a divided highway begins ahead. Keep to the right of the median divider.

questions.question: When is highway pavement most slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain first begins.
After it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain first begins.
questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery when rain first starts. Dirt and oil on the road mix with rainwater to create a slick, greasy surface.

questions.question: How can you avoid glare from an oncoming car's headlights?

options.text: Look toward the right side of the road.
Look at the centerline of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights from an oncoming vehicle. After a brief glance to the side, continue looking ahead to track the other vehicle's position.

questions.question: If dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should drive slowly and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly. Other drivers may also have trouble seeing you, so your headlights help them see your vehicle.

questions.question: For quick turns, your hands should be:

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other at the top of the steering wheel.
On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This grip is comfortable and allows you to turn safely on highways at high speeds.

questions.question: Which statement about work zones is true?

options.text: Fines for work zone violations are the same as regular traffic violations.
You must slow down for work zones.
Slow down only if you see workers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down for work zones.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed in work zones and be ready to stop for highway equipment. Driving carefully through work zones keeps drivers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and road workers safe.

questions.question: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians crossing the street, whether in a marked or unmarked crosswalk. To be safe, yield to anyone crossing any street.

questions.question: When should you be most careful turning or stopping in rain?

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful turning and stopping during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars has not yet washed away and mixes with rainwater to create a slippery surface.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the road edge, you should:

options.text: Slow down, check traffic, then gradually return to the road when safe.
Turn back onto the road immediately.
Stop right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, check traffic, then gradually return to the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back onto the road immediately if your wheels drop off. Instead, reduce your speed, check traffic, and gradually steer back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.question: When exiting the interstate, when should you start slowing down?

options.text: Halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you approach the deceleration lane.
Right when you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Stay at your current speed until you enter the deceleration lane. Then reduce your speed to the posted speed for the exit ramp.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and proceed with caution.
Look to the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Pass stopped vehicles slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the left and right sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Look to the left and right of your vehicle when approaching places where people may cross your path or where traffic lines meet. This helps you see what is coming.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should not:

options.text: Continue to the next exit and find another way to your destination.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your correct exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on the road or shoulder if you miss an exit. Continue to the next exit or crossroad. Drivers do not expect a vehicle backing up and collisions are likely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: School zone or crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign warns drivers of a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: As a vehicle's speed increases, stopping distance and collision severity:

options.text: Decrease.
Stay the same.
Increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: Speeding causes serious problems. As speed increases, stopping distance increases and collisions become more severe, raising the risk of serious injury or death. Increase your following distance as you speed up.

questions.question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if the:

options.text: Vehicle ahead moves right to let you pass.
Yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
Yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side may pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light. If you have not entered yet, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through before the light turns red.
Slow down and carefully proceed through the intersection.
Come to a safe stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a safe stop.
questions.explanation: Stop safely when you see a steady yellow light and have not yet entered the intersection. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through safely.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within the light from your headlights.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead.
Keep dashboard lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within the light from your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: On a road with a single broken white centerline, you:

options.text: Must stay in your lane.
May cross the centerline to change lanes.
May change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: May cross the centerline to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction. A broken white line means you may pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.
